title: Science Says These Are The Most Pleasing Names To Hear
titleZh: 起什么样的名字最讨人喜欢？科学家有答案了
summary:
你有没有注意到，有些名字会让人心生好感，而有些名字却会让人起鸡皮疙瘩？比如，Luke或Leia这样的名字，可能会让你不禁嘴角上扬。Rocky或Taylor，听起来也许会让你感到振奋；但如果是Donald或Hillary，可能就会让你下意识地皱起眉头。

来源：Yourtango；作者：Bill Sullivan Jr.；原文发布时间：2025-07-31 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Have you ever noticed how some names make you smile while others make you shudder? Luke or Leia may stir feelings of happiness. Rocky or Taylor may spark inspiration. Donald or Hillary might make you cringe.
paragraphs.contentZh: 你有没有注意到，有些名字会让人心生好感，而有些名字却会让人起鸡皮疙瘩？比如，Luke或Leia这样的名字，可能会让你不禁嘴角上扬。Rocky或Taylor，听起来也许会让你感到振奋；但如果是Donald或Hillary，可能就会让你下意识地皱起眉头。

paragraphs.contentEn: Many parents agonize over what to name their child because they realize that it is often the basis of a first impression. Names made famous (or infamous) because of celebrity in fiction or the real world may unconsciously rouse emotions tied to that character. Disturbingly, names can also provoke implicit bias against individuals based on racial and ethnic stereotypes.
paragraphs.contentZh: 许多父母在为孩子取名时都十分纠结，因为他们意识到，名字往往决定了他人对孩子的第一印象。那些因现实中的名人或虚构角色而声名在外（或名声不佳）的名字，可能会在不经意间唤起人们与之相关的情绪联想。更令人担忧的是，名字有时还会因涉及特定种族或族裔的刻板印象，引发对个体的潜在偏见。

paragraphs.contentEn: Unique names are on the rise despite studies suggesting that common names bestow significant advantages. Because they are familiar, simple, and common names tend to breed trust and camaraderie. One study showed that we are more altruistic to those who share our name. Another showed that immigrants who Americanized their names were more successful in their new country. Other potential downsides to a unique name include the pressure to stand out from the crowd or narcissism.
paragraphs.contentZh: 尽管有研究表明，常见名字往往能带来诸多优势，但选择独特名字的趋势仍在上升。由于更熟悉且易于记忆，常见名字往往更容易赢得他人的信任与亲近。一项研究发现，人们往往更愿意对与自己同名的人施以援手。另一项研究指出，如果移民将自己的名字“美国化”，在异国可能更容易获得成功。相比之下，独特的名字也可能带来一些潜在问题，比如为了与众不同而承受心理压力，或助长自恋倾向。

paragraphs.contentEn: Some researchers have suggested that a person’s name may become a self-fulfilling prophecy, predicting their vocation later in life. This concept is called nominative determinism. Examples include someone named Art becoming an artist or someone named Butz becoming a proctologist. Another study suggests that people tend to alter their appearance to be in sync with their name.
paragraphs.contentZh: 一些研究人员认为，一个人的名字可能会成为一种自我实现的预言，影响日后的职业选择。这种现象被称为“姓名决定论”。比如，一个叫Art的人后来成为了艺术家，或一个姓Butz（发音近似“屁股”）的人最终成了肛肠科医生。还有研究发现，人们甚至会调整自己的外貌，使其与名字所传达的形象更为一致。

paragraphs.contentEn: Recent studies suggest that the individual sound components of a word, including a person’s name, trigger unconscious feelings in our brain. Certain sounds, or phonemes, seem to carry specific meaning. Researchers have shown that people associate nonwords with certain shapes. Participants associate a made-up word like “bouba” with round shapes and “kiki” with sharp shapes. This phenomenon has been dubbed the Bouba/Kiki effect.
paragraphs.contentZh: 近期的研究发现，某个单词（包括人名在内）的个别发音特征可能会在我们大脑中激起无意识的情感反应。某些声音单位（即音素）似乎自带特定含义。研究人员发现，人们会将没有实际意义的词与某些形状建立关联。例如，实验参与者往往会把“bouba”这样的虚构词与圆润的形状联系起来，而把“kiki”与尖锐的形状联系在一起。这一现象命名为“Bouba/Kiki 效应”。

paragraphs.contentEn: The human brain appears to have been wired through evolution to respond to certain sound waves and rhythms. Particular sounds are crucial for survival; for example, a scream indicates danger while a laugh can diffuse a tense situation. Specific sound waves induce conserved responses in the brain, which raises the idea that a person’s name can elicit universal sensations when heard.
paragraphs.contentZh: 人类的大脑在进化过程中似乎逐渐具备了对特定声波和节奏自动作出反应的机制。某些声音对生存来说至关重要；比如尖叫通常预示危险，而笑声则有助于缓和紧张氛围。特定声波能在大脑中引发相当一致的反应，这也引发了一个设想：一个人的名字，在被听到时，可能也会唤起一种普遍的感受。

paragraphs.contentEn: A 2015 study provided evidence that the sound components within names can produce a Bouba/Kiki effect. How “round” or “sharp” a name sounds can factor into the judgment of that person’s personality. One of the researchers commented, “So a name like Bob or Molly, for example, it’s a bit smoother when you say it versus a name like Kirk or Kate, which kind of has this abruptness to it … People will match those kinds of qualities, like abruptness or smoothness, metaphorically with these traits like being easy going or maybe being rude.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 一项发表于2015年的研究提供了证据，表明名字中的发音特征确实会引发“Bouba/Kiki效应”。一个名字听起来是“圆润”还是“尖锐”，可能会影响人们对名字主人性格的判断。一位研究人员评论道：“举个例子，像Bob或Molly这样的名字，读起来更圆滑顺口，而Kirk或Kate这样的名字听起来则更尖锐……人们往往会用这些声音特质进行联想，将圆润或尖锐与温和随和或生硬刻薄的性格特点对应起来。”

paragraphs.contentEn: What names sound the most pleasing to our ears? Bodo Winter, an associate professor in cognitive linguistics at the University of Birmingham, set out to determine which names sound the “most beautiful” when spoken out loud. He recruited hundreds of diverse individuals to listen to the pronunciation of the most popular names for 2022 in the UK and US.
paragraphs.contentZh: 什么样的名字最能取悦人耳？伯明翰大学认知语言学副教授博多·温特展开了一项研究，试图找出哪些名字在朗读时听起来“最具美感”。他招募了数百名背景各异的参与者，让他们聆听2022年英国和美国最受欢迎的一批名字的发音。

paragraphs.contentEn: Scoring of the names was based on a system devised by James Adelman, who conducted a similar study in 2018 on basic words (not names). Adelman’s findings were consistent with the Bouba/Kiki effect, leading him to conclude that “human languages signal emotions via individual phonemes.” Winter’s study extends Adelman’s findings to common names in the US and UK. Some names are perceived as more pleasing than others, based on the emotional responses to the sounds heard when the name is annunciated.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这些名字的评分参考了詹姆斯·阿德尔曼设计的一套体系，他曾在2018年针对基础词汇（非人名）开展过一项类似研究。阿德尔曼的研究结果与“Bouba/Kiki 效应”一致，因此他提出：“人类语言会通过单个音素传递情感。”温特的研究则在此基础上，进一步将这一结论应用于英美常见的人名。温特的观点是，当名字被清晰读出时，其中的声音会引发人们不同的情感反应，有些名字因此被认为更悦耳动听。

paragraphs.contentEn: Results indicated that Sophia, which means “wisdom” in Greek, is the “most beautiful” sounding name in both countries. Commenting on the result, Winter stated, “The name Sophia contains a combination of sounds that are treated as pleasant by the brain, because of their smoothness and softness.” Zoe placed second for girls in each country. Matthew was the top-ranked name for boys in the US. In the UK, it was Zayn.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究结果显示，在英美两国中，听起来“最悦耳”的名字是Sophia（希腊语中意为“智慧”）。对此结果，温特解释说：“Sophia这个名字的音素组合具有顺滑和柔和的特点，因此更容易被大脑感知为令人愉快的声音。”在女孩名字中，Zoe在两国均位列第二。男孩名字方面，美国排名第一的是Matthew。英国则是Zayn。

paragraphs.contentEn: I was happy to see my name on both lists, although I go by Bill and not William. Maybe I should change that? While these studies suggest that our subconscious starts to make assumptions about people based on their name alone, it is crucial that we never judge a book by its cover. Be aware of your unconscious bias and get to know someone’s character before leaping to conclusions about them.
paragraphs.contentZh: 看到自己的名字同时出现在这两份榜单上，我挺高兴的——不过我平时更常用的是Bill，而不是William。也许我该改过来了？尽管这些研究表明，我们的潜意识往往会仅凭名字就对一个人产生预设印象，但关键的一点是，我们绝不能“以貌取人”。所以要意识到自己的无意识偏见，并在真正了解一个人的性格之前，不要贸然下结论。
